Header: Busseola fusca , Eldana saccharina and Chilo partellus

Prevention: Burn or deep bury the maize debris after harvest
Rotate maize with non-host plants, especially non-cereals (beans, cassava, sweet potato, soybean etc)
Plant maize and cowpea/or desmodium in the same garden to reduce the numbers of caterpillars
Collect and bury attacked stems or feed them to animals
Plant elephant grass around the field to attract the larvae of stalk borers
Plant your maize and sorghum at the onset of rain so that the maize passes the most preferred stage of the caterpillar
Monitoring: Start looking for signs and symptoms of damage when plants are 2 to 4 weeks old, depending on the area.
If you find damage holes in the leaves then constitute a control program
Direct Control: Mix dry clay or sawdust with small neem ( Azadirachta indica ) powder (ground neem seeds) at a rate of 1:1 and place in the funnel of the plant
Handpick and kill caterpillars found on plants
Restrictions: Consult your extension worker and always read the label for direction on use.
Always wear protective gear (overalls, gumboots, goggles, caps, gloves and face masks) when handling chemicals
